title: NULL, Three-Valued Logic, and IS NULL Operator
description: Learn about NULL values, three-valued logic, and how to use the IS NULL and IS NOT NULL operators to test for NULL in SQL Server.

data.text: NULL, Three-Valued Logic, and IS NULL Operator
In the database world, NULL is used to indicate the absence of any data value. For example, when recording customer information, the email may be unknown, so you record it as NULL in the database.

Typically, the result of a logical expression is TRUE or FALSE. However, when NULL is involved in the logical evaluation, the result can be UNKNOWN. Therefore, a logical expression may return one of three values: TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN. This is called three-valued logic.
The results of the following comparisons are all UNKNOWN:

data.title: NULL Comparisons
data.content: NULL does not equal anything, not even itself.

data.text: The NULL does not equal anything, not even itself. This is because each NULL could be a different value. Therefore, NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN rather than TRUE.
To test whether a value is NULL or not, you always use the IS NULL operator. Using WHERE phone = NULL does not work because it evaluates to UNKNOWN.

data.title: Incorrect NULL Test
data.content: Using = NULL returns an empty result set because it evaluates to UNKNOWN.
data.code:
SELECT
    customer_id,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    phone
FROM
    sales.customers
WHERE
    phone = NULL
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.title: Common Mistake
data.text: Never use the = operator to test for NULL. The expression phone = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, and the WHERE clause only returns rows where the predicate evaluates to TRUE.

data.title: Correct NULL Test with IS NULL
data.content: Use IS NULL to find rows where the value is NULL.
data.code:
SELECT
    customer_id,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    phone
FROM
    sales.customers
WHERE
    phone IS NULL
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.text: The query returned the customers who did not have phone information.
To check if a value is not NULL, you can use the IS NOT NULL operator:

data.title: IS NOT NULL Example
data.content: Find customers who have phone numbers recorded.
data.code:
SELECT
    customer_id,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    phone
FROM
    sales.customers
WHERE
    phone IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NULL indicates the absence of data or unknown information.
Three-valued logic allows expressions to evaluate to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN.
NULL does not equal anything, not even itself.
Use IS NULL to test if a value is NULL; never use the = operator.
Use IS NOT NULL to test if a value is not NULL.
